analysis.title: Macro Outlook 2027: Steady Baseline, Downside Risks (Webcast Presentation, 12 November 2026)
key_insights: GS's baseline for 2027 is steady growth with downside risks. Its global GDP forecast is slightly above potential.
A further rise in oil prices from Middle East escalation could derail the growth outlook. The deck separately shows a variable risk premium in oil markets.
Higher rates could lead to a pullback in activity, which is a second downside risk to growth.
Markets have stopped rewarding higher AI capex, and upward revisions to AI capex have slowed.
The AI impulse has contributed much more to US earnings growth and market value than to US GDP growth.
S&P 500 total earnings are at a record high relative to GDP.
AI productivity gains are starting to create broader hiring headwinds. The deck's regressions link higher AI adoption by industry to a higher unemployment rate and weaker employment growth.
Temporary drivers of core PCE inflation (software and accessories mismeasurement, an energy/Iran effect and tariffs) should recede in 2027.
GS forecasts further tightening for most DM central banks. Its forecasts are generally dovish relative to market pricing on a risk-adjusted basis.

The shifting dominance between AI worries and oil worries has changed yield correlations. A shift from energy pressure to AI pressure has produced more negative equity-bond correlations and improved the hedging value of bonds.
GS's baseline forecasts are for positive returns in both equities and bonds in 2027. The downside risks support diversification and hedging.
earnings_insights: S&P 500 total earnings are at a record high relative to GDP. No company-level figures are given in the text.

macro_indicators.reading: Slightly above potential (GS vs consensus forecasts for 2026, 2027 and 2028 are charted in a table, but the extracted text does not label the columns reliably)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Baseline is steady growth. The deck flags oil and higher rates as the main downside risks.

macro_indicators.reading: Software mismeasurement, energy/Iran and tariff effects are charted as temporary drivers that fade through 2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: GS expects the temporary contributions to year-over-year core PCE to recede in 2027.

macro_indicators.reading: Further tightening forecast for most DM central banks
macro_indicators.interpretation: GS's path is generally dovish relative to market pricing on a risk-adjusted basis.

risk_factors: A further rise in oil prices from Middle East escalation.
Higher rates leading to a pullback in activity.
Markets no longer rewarding higher AI capex, with upward revisions slowing.
AI-driven productivity gains creating broader hiring headwinds.
charts_described: Chart of 1-week and 1-month S&P 500/10Y US Treasury correlations from Dec-25 to Oct-26 on a -0.8 to 0.8 scale, titled as showing more negative equity-bond correlations as AI pressure replaced energy pressure.
Chart of effects of temporary factors (software and accessories mismeasurement, energy/Iran, tariffs) on year-over-year core PCE inflation, Jan-25 to Jan-28, with a GS forecast segment.
vol_and_positioning: The 1-week and 1-month S&P 500/10Y US Treasury correlations moved more negative as AI pressure replaced energy pressure as the dominant worry, which improved the hedging value of bonds.
GS says downside risks support diversification and hedging despite positive baseline returns for equities and bonds.
geopolitical: Middle East escalation could push oil prices higher and derail the growth outlook.
An energy/Iran effect is a temporary contributor to core PCE inflation that GS expects to recede in 2027.

key_data_points.metric: Fitted relationship between industry AI adoption and unemployment rate change (t-stat 4.13)
key_data_points.context: Cross-industry regression using BTOS AI adoption and BLS/IPUMS data, latest 3m average minus 2015-2019 average.

key_data_points.metric: Fitted relationship between industry AI adoption and employment growth (t-stat -2.53)
key_data_points.context: Same cross-industry regression framework as the unemployment rate fit.

tension_points.bull_case: GS's baseline forecasts are for positive returns in both equities and bonds in 2027, with global growth slightly above potential and temporary inflation drivers receding.
tension_points.bear_case: Downside risks from oil, higher rates and AI pressure support diversification and hedging. Markets have stopped rewarding higher AI capex.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further rise in oil prices from Middle East escalation, which the deck says could derail the growth outlook.
